question:
Which of the following idioms given in the alternatives has the meaning?

To be very close friends who share a strong, sometimes secretive, bond with each other.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. As thick as thieves.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "As thick as thieves" means to be very close, extremely intimate and loyal friends who share everything with one another.
◦ (बहुत घनिष्ठ मित्र होना)

• This idiom is informal and a classic exam idiom and is commonly used to describe two people who are inseparable and often seen together. (यह मुहावरा उन दो लोगों के लिए प्रयोग होता है जो हमेशा साथ रहते हैं)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. As thick as thieves.

 

Additional Information

• Option 2: A fair-weather friend (मतलबी दोस्त): someone who is a friend only when things are going well, and disappears in times of trouble.
◦ Example: He proved to be a fair-weather friend, vanishing the moment I needed support.

• Option 3: Bury the hatchet (मनमुटाव भुलाकर सुलह करना): to end a quarrel or conflict and become friendly again.
◦ Example: After years of rivalry, the two families finally decided to bury the hatchet.

• Option 4: Give the cold shoulder (जानबूझकर उपेक्षा करना): to deliberately behave in an unfriendly way towards someone by ignoring them.
◦ Example: Ever since their disagreement, she has been giving him the cold shoulder.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. A bad patch – Difficult period (कठिन समय)

2. Add fuel to the fire – To make a bad situation even worse (आग में घी डालना)

3. Back to the drawing board – To start planning something again from the beginning (नए सिरे से शुरुआत करना)

4. Barking up the wrong tree – Pursuing a mistaken or misguided course of action (गलत दिशा में प्रयास करना)

5. Bite the bullet – To face a difficult or unpleasant situation with courage (साहस के साथ कठिनाई का सामना करना)

question:
Fill in the blank with the correct idiom selecting from the given alternatives.

With only two hours left before the deadline, the entire team worked ______ to finish the report.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Against the clock.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "against the clock" means to work quickly and under time pressure in order to finish something before a deadline, often racing against a limited amount of time. (समय की कमी में जल्दी-जल्दी काम करना)
◦ Example: The doctors worked against the clock to save the accident victim's life.

 

• The completed sentence reads: With only two hours left before the deadline, the entire team worked against the clock to finish the report. This fits because the team had very little time and had to hurry to complete the task.

 

• The expression comes from the image of racing a ticking clock as though it were a competitor, an idea popularised in early twentieth-century sports and radio commentary.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The remaining alternatives — "Against the watch", "Against the calendar" and "Against the hourglass" — are not established English idioms at all. Each has been formed by simply replacing "clock" with another timekeeping device, and none of them carries any accepted meaning in English.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Break the ice – To initiate conversation in a social setting (बातचीत की शुरुआत करना)

2. Burn the midnight oil – To work late into the night (देर रात तक मेहनत करना)

3. By the skin of one's teeth – To narrowly escape a difficult situation (बाल-बाल बचना)

4. Call it a day – To stop working on something for the day (काम बंद करना)

5. Cost an arm and a leg – To be extremely expensive (बहुत महंगा होना)

question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct meaning of the idiom.

Beat around the bush.
option_1: To search thoroughly through dense vegetation for something lost.
option_2: To hunt for small animals hiding in bushes.
option_3: To avoid talking directly about the main subject, often by discussing irrelevant details first.
option_4: To argue loudly and aggressively about an issue.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. To avoid talking directly about the main subject, often by discussing irrelevant details first..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "beat around the bush" means to avoid talking directly about the main point of a matter, often by discussing unrelated or minor details instead. (मुख्य विषय पर सीधे बात न करना)
◦ Example: Stop beating around the bush and tell me exactly what happened.

 

• The idiom is often confused with simply being evasive or indecisive, but its special sense lies in the word "beat", which recalls hunters beating bushes to flush out game before addressing the real target — the actual matter at hand.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 describes a literal search through bushes, which is not what this idiom refers to — it is figurative, about avoiding a topic, not searching for a lost object.

 

• Option 2 takes the word "bush" too literally, as if it were about hunting animals; the idiom has nothing to do with actual bushes or animals.

 

• Option 4 confuses this idiom with expressions about arguing forcefully; "beat around the bush" actually describes evasiveness and delay, not aggression.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Cry over spilt milk – To regret something that has already happened and cannot be changed (बीती बात पर पछताना)

2. Cut corners – To do something in the cheapest or easiest way, often sacrificing quality (काम में कोताही बरतना)

3. Down to earth – Practical, sensible and modest in manner (सीधा-सादा और व्यावहारिक)

4. Draw a blank – To fail to find an answer or recall something (कुछ याद न आना)

5. Eat humble pie – To admit a mistake and apologise humbly (अपनी गलती विनम्रतापूर्वक स्वीकार करना)

question:
Which of the following idioms given in the alternatives has the meaning?

Whatever makes a person happy or satisfied, used to say that people are free to do or like whatever they wish, even if it is unusual.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Whatever floats your boat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Whatever floats your boat" means whatever makes a person happy or satisfied, used to show that everyone is free to choose what they enjoy.
◦ (जो भी तुम्हें पसंद हो / जो तुम्हें अच्छा लगे)

• This idiom is informal and conversational and is commonly used to express casual acceptance of someone else's personal choice or preference. (यह मुहावरा किसी की व्यक्तिगत पसंद को सहजता से स्वीकार करने के लिए प्रयोग होता है)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Whatever floats your boat.

 

Additional Information

• Option 1: Miss the boat (मौका चूक जाना): to lose an opportunity by being too slow to act.
◦ Example: If you don't apply today, you'll miss the boat on this scholarship.

• Option 2: Rock the boat (स्थिति को अस्थिर करना): to disturb a stable situation or cause trouble unnecessarily.
◦ Example: Everyone was happy with the plan, so he decided not to rock the boat.

• Option 3: Burn your boats (वापसी का रास्ता बंद कर देना): to commit fully to a course of action, making it impossible to return to a previous state.
◦ Example: By resigning before securing a new job, she had well and truly burnt her boats.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Face the music – To accept the unpleasant consequences of one's actions (परिणाम भुगतना)

2. Get cold feet – To become nervous or hesitant about doing something (हिम्मत हार जाना)

3. Go the extra mile – To make a greater effort than is expected (अतिरिक्त प्रयास करना)

4. Hit the nail on the head – To describe exactly what is causing a situation (एकदम सही बात कहना)

5. In the same boat – To be in the same difficult situation as someone else (एक ही स्थिति में होना)

question:
Fill in the blank with the correct idiom selecting from the given alternatives.

"______," she said, promising not to breathe a word about the surprise party to anyone.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Mum's the word.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "mum's the word" means to stay silent about something, especially a secret, and not tell anyone about it. (चुप रहना / राज़ न खोलना)
◦ Example: Mum's the word about the surprise party — don't tell Rita anything!

 

• The completed sentence reads: "Mum's the word," she said, promising not to breathe a word about the surprise party to anyone. This fits because she is agreeing to keep the secret and stay silent.

 

• The expression comes from the Middle English word "mum", meaning silence (the sound made with closed lips), and has been used in this sense since Shakespeare's time.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The remaining alternatives — "Dad's the word", "Aunt's the word" and "Sister's the word" — are not established English idioms at all. Each has been formed by simply replacing "mum" with another family member, and none of them carries any accepted meaning in English.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Jump on the bandwagon – To join a popular activity or trend (लोकप्रिय प्रवृत्ति में शामिल होना)

2. Keep an eye on – To watch someone or something carefully (ध्यान रखना)

3. Kill two birds with one stone – To achieve two things with a single action (एक तीर से दो शिकार करना)

4. Let the cat out of the bag – To reveal a secret accidentally (राज़ खोल देना)

5. Make a mountain out of a molehill – To exaggerate a minor problem into something serious (राई का पहाड़ बनाना)

question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct meaning of the idiom.

At sixes and sevens.
option_1: Arranged neatly in a numerical sequence.
option_2: In a state of total confusion or disorder.
option_3: Having exactly thirteen items in total.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. In a state of total confusion or disorder..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "at sixes and sevens" means in a state of total confusion or disorder, with everything disorganised and out of place. (पूरी तरह अव्यवस्थित / गड़बड़ में)
◦ Example: After the sudden power cut, the whole office was at sixes and sevens.

 

• The idiom has nothing to do with actual numbers; its origin is often traced to an old dice game, and today it is used purely to describe confusion and disarray, not any numerical count.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 wrongly assumes the idiom describes neat numerical order, when in fact it describes the exact opposite — disorder and confusion.

 

• Option 3 is a literal misreading that treats "six" and "seven" as numbers to be added together, which is not the idiom's figurative sense at all.

 

• Option 4 confuses this idiom with expressions about good fortune; "at sixes and sevens" conveys disorganised confusion, not luck.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Once in a blue moon – Very rarely (कभी-कभार)

2. Out of the blue – Suddenly and unexpectedly (अचानक)

3. Piece of cake – Something that is very easy to do (बहुत आसान काम)

4. Pull someone's leg – To joke with or tease someone (मज़ाक उड़ाना)

5. Rain cats and dogs – To rain very heavily (मूसलधार बारिश होना)

question:
Which of the following idioms given in the alternatives has the meaning?

To compromise with someone by each side giving up part of what they want in order to reach an agreement.
option_1: Draw a line in the sand
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Meet halfway.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Meet halfway" means to compromise with someone, with each side giving up part of what they want to reach a fair agreement.
◦ (समझौता करना / आधे रास्ते पर मिलना)

• This idiom is a common negotiation-related expression and is commonly used in discussions about resolving disputes fairly. (यह मुहावरा विवाद सुलझाने में समझौते की बात करते समय प्रयोग होता है)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Meet halfway.

 

Additional Information

• Option 1: Draw a line in the sand (स्पष्ट सीमा तय करना): to set a firm limit beyond which one will not compromise.
◦ Example: The manager drew a line in the sand and refused to extend the deadline any further.

• Option 2: Stand one's ground (अपनी बात पर अड़े रहना): to refuse to change one's position or give in, despite pressure.
◦ Example: Despite the criticism, she stood her ground and refused to withdraw her proposal.

• Option 4: Put one's foot down (दृढ़तापूर्वक मना करना): to firmly insist on something or refuse to allow it, showing no willingness to compromise.
◦ Example: His father finally put his foot down and refused to lend him the car again.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Read between the lines – To understand a hidden or implied meaning (छिपे हुए अर्थ को समझना)

2. Run out of steam – To lose energy or momentum (ऊर्जा खत्म हो जाना)

3. See eye to eye – To agree completely with someone (पूरी तरह सहमत होना)

4. Spill the beans – To reveal secret information (भेद खोल देना)

5. Take with a grain of salt – To not take something too seriously or literally (संदेह के साथ लेना)

question:
Fill in the blank with the correct idiom selecting from the given alternatives.

Rather than supporting either candidate, the councillor chose to ______ throughout the entire debate.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Sit on the fence.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "sit on the fence" means to remain neutral or avoid taking sides in a dispute or decision, refusing to commit to either option. (तटस्थ रहना / किसी पक्ष में न होना)
◦ Example: The senator has been sitting on the fence on this controversial bill for weeks.

 

• The completed sentence reads: Rather than supporting either candidate, the councillor chose to sit on the fence throughout the entire debate. This fits because the councillor avoided committing to either side.

 

• The expression comes from the image of a person literally perched on top of a fence, unable to decide which side of a field to come down on.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The remaining alternatives — "Sit on the wall", "Sit on the wire" and "Sit on the rail" — are not established English idioms at all. Each has been formed by simply replacing "fence" with another similar structure, and none of them carries any accepted meaning in English.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. The ball is in your court – It is now your turn to take action or make a decision (अब निर्णय तुम्हारा है)

2. Throw in the towel – To give up on something (हार मान लेना)

3. Under the weather – Feeling slightly unwell (तबीयत ठीक न होना)

4. Up in the air – Undecided or uncertain (अनिश्चित)

5. Wear your heart on your sleeve – To openly show one's emotions (भावनाएँ खुलकर दिखाना)

question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct meaning of the idiom.

Keep her nose to the grindstone.
option_1: To work hard and continuously without stopping, applying oneself diligently to a task.
option_2: To literally grind one's nose against a stone tool for sharpening.
option_3: To smell something unpleasant very closely.
option_4: To complain persistently about a difficult task.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. To work hard and continuously without stopping, applying oneself diligently to a task..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "keep her nose to the grindstone" means to work hard and continuously at a task, without stopping to rest. (लगातार कड़ी मेहनत करना)
◦ Example: Ever since she started her own business, she has kept her nose to the grindstone to make it succeed.

 

• The idiom can be used with any subject (his/their/one's nose to the grindstone); the word "grindstone" — a stone once used to sharpen tools — is what gives the idiom its sense of continuous, wearing effort.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 takes the idiom completely literally, imagining an actual grindstone being used on someone's nose, which is not its figurative meaning.

 

• Option 3 wrongly focuses on the word "nose" as related to smell, when the idiom is actually about persistent hard work, not the sense of smell.

 

• Option 4 confuses hard work with complaining; "keep her nose to the grindstone" is about diligent effort, not grumbling about a task.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. A blessing in disguise – Something that seems bad at first but turns out to be good (मुसीबत में भी फ़ायदा)

2. A drop in the ocean – A very small amount compared to what is needed (ऊँट के मुँह में जीरा)

3. A penny for your thoughts – A way of asking what someone is thinking (तुम क्या सोच रहे हो)

4. A piece of one's mind – To tell someone frankly what one thinks, usually in anger (खरी-खरी सुनाना)

5. Actions speak louder than words – What a person does matters more than what they say (करनी कथनी से बड़ी होती है)

question:
Which of the following idioms given in the alternatives has the meaning?

Operating or accomplishing something with very little money, on a very tight budget.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. On a shoestring.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "On a shoestring" means to do something with very little money, on a very tight or limited budget.
◦ (बहुत कम पैसों में / तंगहाली में)

• This idiom is informal and frequently used in business and travel contexts and is commonly used to describe frugal or low-cost ventures. (यह मुहावरा कम खर्च में कोई काम करने के लिए प्रयोग होता है)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. On a shoestring.

 

Additional Information

• Option 1: In the red (घाटे में / कर्ज़ में): to be in debt or operating at a financial loss.
◦ Example: The company has been in the red for the past two quarters.

• Option 3: Break the bank (बहुत अधिक खर्च कर देना): to cost far more money than one can afford, or to use up all of one's money.
◦ Example: A weekend trip to the city won't exactly break the bank.

• Option 4: Money to burn (बहुत अधिक पैसा होना): to have a great deal of money to spend freely, more than one needs.
◦ Example: After winning the lottery, he acted as if he had money to burn.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Add insult to injury – To make a bad situation even worse (जले पर नमक छिड़कना)

2. All ears – Listening eagerly and attentively (पूरे ध्यान से सुनना)

3. Barking mad – Completely crazy (पूरी तरह पागल)

4. Best of both worlds – The advantages of two different things at the same time (दोनों जगह का लाभ)

5. Bite off more than you can chew – To take on more responsibility than one can handle (क्षमता से अधिक काम अपने ऊपर लेना)

question:
Fill in the blank with the correct idiom selecting from the given alternatives.

Once a household name in the industry, the company has largely ______ in recent years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Fallen off the radar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "fallen off the radar" means to no longer be noticed, tracked, or paid attention to by others, having faded from public or general awareness. (ध्यान से ओझल हो जाना / नज़रों से गायब हो जाना)
◦ Example: After retiring from politics, the former minister largely fell off the radar.

 

• The completed sentence reads: Once a household name in the industry, the company has largely fallen off the radar in recent years. This fits because the company is no longer prominent or noticed the way it once was.

 

• The expression comes from radar tracking technology, where an object that is no longer detected on the radar screen is said to have "fallen off" it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The remaining alternatives — "Gone off the rails" (to start behaving in an uncontrolled or unacceptable way), "Fallen from grace" (to lose the respect or favour one previously enjoyed, usually after a mistake or scandal) and "Gone off the grid" (to deliberately cut oneself off from modern communication and society) — are all genuine idioms, but none of them fits the sense of fading from notice or attention required by this sentence.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Bring to the table – To contribute something valuable to a discussion or project (कुछ मूल्यवान योगदान देना)

2. Cut to the chase – To get to the point without wasting time (सीधे मुद्दे पर आना)

3. Devil's advocate – To argue an opposing view just to test an idea (जानबूझकर विरोधी पक्ष लेना)

4. Don't count your chickens before they hatch – Don't assume success before it actually happens (सफलता से पहले उसका अनुमान मत लगाओ)

5. Every cloud has a silver lining – There is something good hidden in every bad situation (हर बुरी चीज़ में कुछ अच्छाई छिपी होती है)

question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct meaning of the idiom.

Pain in the neck.
option_1: A sharp, sudden physical ache felt specifically in the neck muscles.
option_2: A short and effortless way of completing a difficult task.
option_3: A minor problem that resolves itself without any effort or attention.
option_4: A person or thing that is extremely annoying or troublesome.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. A person or thing that is extremely annoying or troublesome..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "Pain in the neck" means a person or thing that is extremely annoying or troublesome, causing constant irritation. (किसी व्यक्ति या वस्तु के लिए जो लगातार परेशान करे)
◦ Example: My noisy neighbour who plays loud music every night is a real pain in the neck.

 

• The word "pain" is used figuratively here for irritation, not for any actual physical ache, so the phrase must never be read literally.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 takes the words literally, treating "pain" as an actual physical ache in the neck rather than the figurative sense of annoyance.

 

• Option 2 wrongly borrows the sense of an idiom like "a piece of cake", which describes ease, the exact opposite of what this idiom conveys.

 

• Option 3 incorrectly suggests a trivial, self-resolving issue, whereas the idiom actually points to a persistent, ongoing source of irritation.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. A bolt from the blue – A sudden, unexpected event (आकस्मिक घटना)

2. Break the ice – To start a conversation in a social setting (बातचीत की शुरुआत करना)

3. Once in a blue moon – Very rarely (कभी-कभार)

4. Under the weather – Feeling slightly unwell (थोड़ा अस्वस्थ महसूस करना)

5. A piece of cake – A very easy task (बहुत आसान काम)

question:
Which of the following idioms given in the alternatives has the meaning?

A great deal of fuss or excitement made over a trivial or unimportant matter.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. A storm in a teacup.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "A storm in a teacup" means a great deal of fuss or excitement made over a trivial or unimportant matter.
◦ (छोटी सी बात पर बड़ा हंगामा)

• This idiom is a classic exam idiom and is commonly used to describe office or family disputes that turn out to be far less serious than they first appeared. (यह एक क्लासिक परीक्षा मुहावरा है और छोटे विवादों को बड़ा बताने के लिए प्रयोग होता है)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. A storm in a teacup.

 

Additional Information

• Option 2: Weather the storm (कठिन समय को सहन करना): to endure a difficult period without giving up.
◦ Example: The small business managed to weather the storm during the economic downturn.

• Option 3: Under a cloud (संदेह के घेरे में): suspected of wrongdoing or in disgrace.
◦ Example: The manager resigned under a cloud after the audit revealed irregularities.

• Option 4: A fair-weather friend (मतलबी दोस्त): someone who is friendly only when things are going well.
◦ Example: He turned out to be a fair-weather friend who disappeared the moment I needed help.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Hit the nail on the head – To say something exactly right (ठीक बात कहना)

2. Let the cat out of the bag – To reveal a secret accidentally (राज़ खोलना)

3. On cloud nine – Extremely happy (बेहद खुश)

4. Burn the midnight oil – To work late into the night (देर रात तक मेहनत करना)

5. A drop in the ocean – A very small amount compared to what is needed (ऊंट के मुंह में जीरा)

question:
Fill in the blank with the correct idiom selecting from the given alternatives.

Ravi was confident that the news was accurate because he had heard it ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. straight from the horse's mouth.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "straight from the horse's mouth" means information obtained directly from the most reliable or original source, leaving no room for doubt. (सीधे विश्वसनीय स्रोत से प्राप्त जानकारी)
◦ Example: I know the transfer is confirmed because I got it straight from the horse's mouth — my manager told me himself.

 

• The completed sentence reads: Ravi was confident that the news was accurate because he had heard it straight from the horse's mouth. This fits because the sentence is about trusting information that came directly from a reliable, firsthand source.

 

• The expression comes from horse racing, where information about a horse's fitness was considered most reliable when it came directly from those closest to the horse, such as its trainer or stable staff.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The remaining alternatives — "straight from the donkey's mouth", "straight from the horse's tail" and "straight from the camel's mouth" — are not established English idioms at all. Each has been formed by simply replacing the animal or body part in the original phrase with a similar substitute, and none of them carries any accepted meaning in English.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. A bad patch – A difficult or unlucky period of time (कठिन समय)

2. A red-letter day – A memorable and important day (यादगार दिन)

3. Apple of one's eye – A person who is dearly loved above all others (आँखों का तारा)

4. Back to the drawing board – To start planning something again from the beginning (नए सिरे से योजना बनाना)

5. At loggerheads – In strong disagreement with someone (तीव्र मतभेद में)

question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct meaning of the idiom.

Bite the bullet.
option_1: To avoid a difficult situation by delaying action indefinitely.
option_2: To complain loudly about a painful experience.
option_3: To bravely face or endure a difficult or unpleasant situation that cannot be avoided.
option_4: To take a small, quick bite of food before an important event.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. To bravely face or endure a difficult or unpleasant situation that cannot be avoided..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "Bite the bullet" means to bravely face or endure a painful or difficult situation that cannot be avoided, often by making a firm decision to go through with it. (किसी कठिन परिस्थिति का साहसपूर्वक सामना करना)
◦ Example: After months of hesitation, she finally bit the bullet and resigned from her toxic workplace.

 

• The idiom is believed to originate from soldiers biting on a bullet to endure pain during surgery without anaesthesia, which is why "bite" carries the sense of enduring pain rather than literally eating something.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 describes the opposite of the idiom's meaning, suggesting avoidance and delay rather than facing the difficulty head-on.

 

• Option 2 confuses the idiom with simply expressing pain or complaint, whereas the idiom is about enduring hardship with courage, not complaining.

 

• Option 4 takes the word "bite" literally, as if it were about eating, which has nothing to do with the idiom's actual figurative meaning.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Cost an arm and a leg – To be extremely expensive (बहुत महंगा होना)

2. Rule of thumb – A general practical principle (सामान्य व्यावहारिक नियम)

3. Spill the beans – To reveal secret information (भेद खोलना)

4. Throw in the towel – To give up on an effort (हार मान लेना)

5. Face the music – To accept the consequences of one's actions (परिणाम भुगतना)

question:
Which of the following idioms given in the alternatives has the meaning?

To unintentionally offend or upset someone, especially by interfering in matters that are their responsibility.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Tread on your toes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Tread on your toes" means to unintentionally offend or upset someone, especially by interfering in matters that are their responsibility.
◦ (किसी के अधिकार क्षेत्र में दखल देकर उसे नाराज़ करना)

• This idiom is a common workplace expression and is commonly used when someone interferes in an area that is not their responsibility. (यह मुहावरा तब प्रयोग होता है जब कोई व्यक्ति दूसरे के कार्यक्षेत्र में हस्तक्षेप करता है)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Tread on your toes.

 

Additional Information

• Option 1: Keep someone at arm's length (किसी से दूरी बनाए रखना): to avoid becoming too closely involved with someone.
◦ Example: After being betrayed once, she preferred to keep new colleagues at arm's length.

• Option 2: Have a change of heart (अपना विचार बदलना): to change one's opinion or decision, usually to a kinder one.
◦ Example: He was going to sue his old friend, but he had a change of heart and dropped the case.

• Option 3: Turn a blind eye (जानबूझकर अनदेखा करना): to deliberately ignore something wrong that is happening.
◦ Example: The supervisor turned a blind eye to the minor rule violations on the factory floor.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Kill two birds with one stone – To achieve two things with a single action (एक तीर से दो निशाने)

2. Get cold feet – To become nervous before doing something important (डर के मारे पीछे हटना)

3. Sit on the fence – To remain neutral in a dispute (तटस्थ रहना)

4. Wild goose chase – A futile and hopeless search or pursuit (व्यर्थ की खोज)

5. Steal someone's thunder – To take credit for another person's achievement (किसी की उपलब्धि का श्रेय खुद ले लेना)

question:
Fill in the blank with the correct idiom selecting from the given alternatives.

The donations for the flood relief fund did not arrive all at once. ______ over several weeks, they trickled in.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. In dribs and drabs.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "in dribs and drabs" means in small, irregular amounts over a period of time, rather than all at once. (थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में समय के साथ)
◦ Example: The old company released its employees' final settlement in dribs and drabs instead of paying the full amount together.

 

• The completed sentence reads: The donations for the flood relief fund did not arrive all at once. In dribs and drabs over several weeks, they trickled in. This fits because the sentence describes money arriving slowly, in small irregular quantities, not in one lump sum.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The remaining alternatives — "In dregs and drabs", "In dribs and grabs" and "In drips and drabs" — are not established English idioms at all. Each has been formed by simply replacing one word in the original phrase with a similar-sounding word, and none of them carries any accepted meaning in English.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. A leopard cannot change its spots – A person's basic nature cannot be changed (स्वभाव कभी नहीं बदलता)

2. Beggars can't be choosers – A person in need must accept what is offered without complaint (जरूरतमंद को नखरे नहीं करने चाहिए)

3. Cry over spilt milk – To waste time regretting something that has already happened and cannot be changed (बीती बात पर पछताना)

4. Down in the dumps – Feeling sad or depressed (उदास होना)

5. Feather in one's cap – An achievement or honour to be proud of (उपलब्धि या सम्मान)

question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct meaning of the idiom.

Take the bull by the horns.
option_1: To avoid a confrontation by staying silent and waiting for the problem to pass.
option_2: To confront a difficult or risky situation directly and with courage.
option_3: To provoke an angry person into an argument deliberately.
option_4: To work on a farm task that requires physical strength.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To confront a difficult or risky situation directly and with courage..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "Take the bull by the horns" means to confront a difficult, risky, or unpleasant situation directly and with courage, rather than avoiding it. (किसी कठिन परिस्थिति का साहस के साथ सीधा सामना करना)
◦ Example: Instead of waiting for the problem to worsen, the new manager decided to take the bull by the horns and restructure the failing department.

 

• The image comes from the dangerous act of grabbing an actual bull's horns to control it, so the idiom always implies deliberate, courageous action, not recklessness or provocation for its own sake.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 describes passive avoidance, which is the opposite of the decisive action the idiom actually describes.

 

• Option 3 wrongly implies deliberately starting a fight or provoking someone, whereas the idiom is about courageously tackling a problem, not picking a quarrel.

 

• Option 4 takes the word "bull" literally, connecting it to farm work, which has nothing to do with the idiom's figurative meaning of boldness.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Add fuel to the fire – To make a bad situation even worse (आग में घी डालना)

2. Beat around the bush – To avoid speaking directly about something (घुमा-फिराकर बात करना)

3. By the skin of one's teeth – Narrowly, by a very small margin (बाल-बाल बचना)

4. Call it a day – To stop doing something for the time being (काम को यहीं समाप्त करना)

5. Every cloud has a silver lining – Something good can be found even in a bad situation (हर मुसीबत में कुछ भलाई छिपी होती है)

question:
Which of the following idioms given in the alternatives has the meaning?

A state of being isolated from the practical realities and problems of everyday life, often associated with academics or intellectuals.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. An ivory tower.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "An ivory tower" means a state of being isolated from the practical realities and problems of everyday life, often associated with academics or intellectuals.
◦ (वास्तविक दुनिया की समस्याओं से अलग-थलग जीवन)

• This idiom is often used critically and is commonly used to describe scholars or officials who are seen as out of touch with ordinary people's struggles. (यह मुहावरा अक्सर उन विद्वानों या अधिकारियों के लिए प्रयोग होता है जो आम लोगों की समस्याओं से कटे हुए हों)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. An ivory tower.

 

Additional Information

• Option 1: A stone's throw (बहुत कम दूरी): a very short distance away.
◦ Example: Their new house is just a stone's throw from the railway station.

• Option 2: Out of the woods (खतरे से बाहर): past a difficult or dangerous stage.
◦ Example: The patient is finally out of the woods after the surgery, said the doctor.

• Option 4: A fish out of water (अपरिचित परिस्थिति में असहज महसूस करना): feeling awkward or uncomfortable in unfamiliar surroundings.
◦ Example: At the formal banquet, the young intern felt like a fish out of water.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Water under the bridge – A past problem that is no longer important (बीती बात, अब महत्वहीन)

2. The last straw – The final small problem that causes a complete collapse of patience (सब्र का आखिरी घूंट)

3. See eye to eye – To fully agree with someone (पूरी तरह सहमत होना)

4. Cast iron stomach – The ability to eat anything without getting sick (कुछ भी पचाने की क्षमता)

5. Elephant in the room – An obvious problem that everyone avoids discussing (वह स्पष्ट समस्या जिसकी चर्चा से सब बचते हैं)

question:
Fill in the blank with the correct idiom selecting from the given alternatives.

The sudden question about her resignation plans left her completely ______, and she struggled to find an answer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. caught off guard.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "caught off guard" means taken by surprise, unprepared for something unexpected, often leaving the person confused momentarily. (अचानक और बिना तैयारी के चौंका देना)
◦ Example: The sudden fire drill caught the entire office off guard during the busiest hour of the day.

 

• The completed sentence reads: The sudden question about her resignation plans left her completely caught off guard, and she struggled to find an answer. This fits because the sentence describes an unexpected question causing surprise and momentary confusion, exactly what the idiom conveys.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The remaining alternatives — "on cloud nine" (extremely happy), "down in the dumps" (feeling sad or depressed) and "up in the air" (undecided or uncertain) — are all genuine idioms, but none of them fits the sense of sudden, unprepared surprise required by this sentence.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. In the same boat – Facing the same difficult situation as someone else (एक ही मुसीबत में होना)

2. Jump on the bandwagon – To join a popular activity or trend (लोकप्रिय प्रवृत्ति में शामिल होना)

3. Lose one's train of thought – To suddenly forget what one was about to say (बात भूल जाना)

4. Make a mountain out of a molehill – To exaggerate a minor problem into a major one (राई का पहाड़ बनाना)

5. Out of the blue – Suddenly and unexpectedly (अचानक)

question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct meaning of the idiom.

Star-crossed lovers.
option_1: Two people in love whose relationship is doomed by fate or bad luck to end in tragedy.
option_2: Two people who fall in love at first sight under a starry night sky.
option_3: Two famous celebrities whose relationship is followed closely by the media.
option_4: Two people who are perfectly matched and destined for a happy, lasting marriage.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Two people in love whose relationship is doomed by fate or bad luck to end in tragedy..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "Star-crossed lovers" means two people in love whose relationship is doomed by fate or bad luck to end unhappily or in tragedy. (भाग्य द्वारा अभिशप्त प्रेमी युगल)
◦ Example: Romeo and Juliet are literature's most famous star-crossed lovers, kept apart by their feuding families.

 

• The phrase comes from the old astrological belief that the position of the stars could bring misfortune, so being "crossed" by unfavourable stars meant being fated to fail, which is why the idiom always carries a tragic, not a romantic-happy, connotation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 wrongly focuses on the literal image of stars in the sky and romantic first meetings, rather than the idiom's actual sense of a fate-doomed relationship.

 

• Option 3 confuses the idiom with celebrity gossip or media attention, which has nothing to do with its meaning of tragic, fate-crossed love.

 

• Option 4 describes the opposite of the idiom's meaning, suggesting a happy destined union rather than a tragic, ill-fated one.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Fit as a fiddle – In very good health (पूर्णतः स्वस्थ)

2. Pull someone's leg – To tease or joke with someone (किसी को मज़ाक में छेड़ना)

3. Give someone the cold shoulder – To deliberately ignore or be unfriendly to someone (जानबूझकर अनदेखा या रूखा व्यवहार करना)

4. Read between the lines – To understand a hidden or implied meaning (छिपे हुए अर्थ को समझना)

5. Go the extra mile – To make a special extra effort to achieve something (अतिरिक्त प्रयास करना)

question:
Which of the following idioms given in the alternatives has the meaning?

An extra, additional benefit or good feature that makes an already good situation even better.
option_4: Have a lot on one's plate
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The icing on the cake.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "The icing on the cake" means an extra, additional benefit or good feature that makes an already good situation even better.
◦ (पहले से अच्छी स्थिति को और भी बेहतर बनाने वाली अतिरिक्त बात)

• This idiom is a positive, food-based expression and is commonly used to describe an unexpected bonus that adds to an already pleasant outcome. (यह मुहावरा किसी पहले से अच्छी स्थिति में मिलने वाले अतिरिक्त लाभ के लिए प्रयोग होता है)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The icing on the cake.

 

Additional Information

• Option 1: A piece of cake (बहुत आसान काम): a task that is very easy to accomplish.
◦ Example: For an experienced driver, parallel parking is a piece of cake.

• Option 3: Bring home the bacon (परिवार के लिए कमाई करना): to earn money to support one's family.
◦ Example: Both parents work night shifts to bring home the bacon for their four children.

• Option 4: Have a lot on one's plate (बहुत सारी जिम्मेदारियां होना): to be very busy or have many responsibilities to handle.
◦ Example: She couldn't join the trip because she already had a lot on her plate at work.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. Cross that bridge when you come to it – To deal with a problem only when it actually arises (जब समस्या आए तभी निपटना)

2. Hold your horses – To wait and be patient (धैर्य रखना)

3. Let sleeping dogs lie – To avoid interfering in a matter that is currently causing no trouble (सोए हुए मामले को मत छेड़ो)

4. On the ball – Alert, competent, and quick to understand things (चौकस और सक्षम)

5. Play devil's advocate – To argue an opposing view deliberately for the sake of debate (जानबूझकर विरोधी पक्ष रखना)

question:
Fill in the blank with the correct idiom selecting from the given alternatives.

The old family mansion, with its crumbling walls and enormous upkeep costs, had become nothing but a ______ for the family.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. A white elephant.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "A white elephant" means a possession that is costly to maintain but has little or no real value, often becoming more of a burden than a benefit. (सफेद हाथी - एक ऐसी वस्तु जो रखरखाव में महंगी हो पर बेकार हो)
◦ Example: The unused sports stadium built for the games turned into a white elephant for the city.

 

• The completed sentence reads: The old family mansion, with its crumbling walls and enormous upkeep costs, had become nothing but a white elephant for the family. The idiom fits because the mansion is expensive to maintain yet serves no useful purpose anymore.

 

• The expression comes from the old Siamese custom of kings gifting rare white elephants to courtiers they wished to burden — the animals were sacred and could not be put to work, yet were extremely costly to keep.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The remaining alternatives — "a cash cow" (a business or asset that generates steady, reliable profit), "a nest egg" (a sum of money saved for future use) and "an old chestnut" (a stale joke or overused idea) — are all genuine idioms, but none of them fits the sense of a costly, useless possession required by this sentence.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. A Bad Patch – Difficult period (कठिन समय)

2. A Bolt From The Blue – A sudden shock (अचानक झटका)

3. A Bone Of Contention – A cause of dispute (विवाद का कारण)

4. A Close Shave – A narrow escape (बाल-बाल बचना)

5. A Far Cry – Very different (बहुत अलग)

question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct meaning of the idiom.

A wild goose chase.
option_1: A hunting expedition organized specifically to catch wild geese.
option_2: A sudden and unexpected event that surprises everyone.
option_3: A competitive race between rival groups.
option_4: A foolish and futile search that has no real chance of succeeding.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. A foolish and futile search that has no real chance of succeeding..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "A wild goose chase" means a foolish and hopeless search or pursuit that wastes time and effort, one that has almost no chance of success. (व्यर्थ की खोज)
◦ Example: Searching for that old email without knowing the sender's name turned into a wild goose chase.

 

• The key trap is treating the phrase literally as an actual chase after geese; in real usage the idiom has nothing to do with birds at all, only with a search that leads nowhere.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 takes the idiom literally, describing an actual hunt for geese, whereas the phrase carries no such literal sense in modern usage.

 

• Option 2 describes a sudden shock, which matches idioms like "a bolt from the blue" rather than a wasted, pointless search.

 

• Option 3 suggests an organised competitive race, but a wild goose chase is aimless and unplanned, not a structured contest.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. A Fish Out Of Water – Uncomfortable in unfamiliar surroundings (असहज महसूस करना)

2. A Green Horn – An inexperienced person (अनुभवहीन व्यक्ति)

3. A Leading Light – An important, influential person (प्रमुख व्यक्ति)

4. A Pain In The Neck – An annoying person or thing (परेशान करने वाला व्यक्ति)

5. A Piece Of Cake – A very easy task (बहुत आसान काम)

question:
Which of the following idioms given in the alternatives has the meaning?

A situation in which everyone available is required to work together to get a task done.
option_2: Too many cooks spoil the broth
option_3: Burn the candle at both ends
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. All hands on deck.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "All hands on deck" means everyone available must pitch in and work together to accomplish a task.
◦ (सब मिलकर काम करना)

• This idiom is nautical in origin and now widely used in everyday and workplace English and is commonly used to call for a full team effort during an emergency or a busy period. (आपातकाल या व्यस्त समय में पूरी टीम के प्रयास का आह्वान करने के लिए प्रयुक्त)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. All hands on deck.

 

Additional Information

• Option 2: Too many cooks spoil the broth (बहुत अधिक लोगों के शामिल होने से काम बिगड़ जाना): means that having too many people involved in a task actually spoils the outcome.
◦ Example: The committee's redesign fell apart because too many cooks spoil the broth.

• Option 3: Burn the candle at both ends (खुद को अत्यधिक परिश्रम से थका देना): means to exhaust oneself by working or partying at all hours without enough rest.
◦ Example: Preparing for exams while working a night job, she was burning the candle at both ends.

• Option 4: Carry the can (किसी और की गलती की जिम्मेदारी लेना): means to take the blame or responsibility for something, often for someone else's mistake.
◦ Example: When the project failed, the young manager had to carry the can for decisions made above him.

 

5 Important Idioms

1. A Rainy Day – A time of future need or trouble (भविष्य की कठिनाई का समय)

2. A Shot In The Arm – A timely boost or encouragement (प्रोत्साहन)

3. A Slap On The Wrist – A very mild punishment (मामूली सजा)

4. A Storm In A Teacup – A great fuss over a trivial matter (छोटी बात पर बड़ा हंगामा)

5. A Wet Blanket – A person who spoils others' fun (उत्साह भंग करने वाला व्यक्ति)
